Uses and Administration Abacavir is a nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor with antiretroviral activity against HIV. It is used in the treatment of HIV infection and AIDS (p.856). Viral re- sistance emerges rapidly when abacavir is used alone, and it is therefore used with other antiretrovirals. Abacavir is given orally as the sulfate but doses are ex- pressed in terms of the base; 1.17 g of abacavir sulfate is equivalent to about 1 g of abacavir. The adult dose is 300 mg twice daily or 600 mg once daily. For details of doses in children, see below. Doses should be reduced in patients with hepatic impairment (see below). Fixed-dose combination products have been devel- oped in order to improve patient adherence and avoid monotherapy, thereby decreasing the risk of acquired drug resistance. Products containing abacavir in com- bination with lamivudine and with lamivudine and zi- dovudine are available in some countries. ◊ Reviews. 1. Hervey PS, Perry CM.
